Today, we are going to learn about how to use a half litre container and a quarter litre container to measure capacity . In this lesson, we will require the following. Five one litre plastic bottles. Get another one little plastic bottle apart from the one we have used above and two half litre plastic bottles. Fill one of the half litre plastic bottle with water. Fill one of the half litre plastic bottle with water. Pour the water into the half litre plastic bottle which is empty, until the levels in the two half little plastic bottles are the same. Pour the water from the first filled half litre plastic bottle into the empty half litre plastic bottle until the levels in the two half litre plastic bottles are the same. Now cut one of the half litre plastic bottles at the level of water to make a quarter litre bottle. Cut one of the half litre plastic bottles at the level of the water to make a quarter litre bottle. Very good learner. We now have a half litre container and a quarter litre container. We have a half litre container and a quarter litre container. The following activity will help you understand more about measuring capacity using a half litre container or a quarter litre container. The following activity will help you understand more about measuring capacity using a half litre container and a quarter litre container. How many half litres are in each of the following? How many half litres are in each of the following? A. One litre. One litre. B. Ten litres. Ten litres. C. five litres. Five Litres. D. Two litres. Two Litres. Learner. How many quarter litres are in each of the following? A one litre. One litre. B. Two Litres. Two Litres. C. three litres. Three litres. D. six litres. six Litres. With that, we come to the end of our lesson today. Share your answers with your parents, guardian or friends. Until you meet again. Goodbye. That was a mathematics program for grade four learners.
